title: Bayesian optimization improves printed BiSbTe thermoelectrics
summary: Learned models guided ink formulation and printing settings for known BiSbTe-based material. The resulting printed samples reached a reported room-temperature zT of 1.3. This is an experimental processing result, rather than discovery of a new chemical composition or demonstrated deployed-device efficiency. The result was public in the July 2024 preprint before the journal version.
ai_technology: Gaussian-process regression and constrained Bayesian optimization
organization: University of Notre Dame; Marquette University

evidence.tested: Printed samples were characterized after model-guided processing.
evidence.unknown: Generality, industrial manufacturing and the contribution of each downstream processing step remain unestablished in this review.
evidence.ai_role: Gaussian-process regression and constrained Bayesian optimization supported the stated study; experimental and interpretive work remained with researchers.

source_review.scope: Primary preprint abstract, submission history and selected PDF passages on model and affiliations.
